statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk sits in the low band on a compressed, two-sided overnight Nasdaq-100 futures session, while Stress stays elevated on a 24-year-high long end, crude above $90 and an active Strait of Hormuz tanker campaign.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The single elevated window in this assessment is 18:00-21:00 UTC, covering the FOMC minutes and the delayed repricing that can follow them, where the mapped state shifts to WATCH.
headline: Nasdaq-100 balanced overnight near record highs; September FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the day's narrow risk window
body: Observed evidence at the assessment time: NQ December futures trade near 31,467, about -0.05%, inside an unusually compressed overnight range of roughly 18 points, and the NAS100 contract is similarly flat. Cash NDX closed Oct 6 at 31,224.69, up 0.48% for a back-to-back record close, but it finished well off its 31,361.37 intraday record, so a meaningful retracement did occur rather than a hold at the extreme. VIX settled at 15.01, down 3.3%. None of the Tail amplifiers from the contract are present: there is no persistent directional efficiency, no shallow-pullback sequence, and no repeated extension after failed retracements. Cross-asset signals conflict rather than align, with U.S. futures flat while Nikkei, Hang Seng and DAX futures sit 0.6% to 0.9% lower, which raises uncertainty more than it raises Tail. The backdrop nevertheless justifies elevated Stress. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5.31% after touching a 24-year high at 5.35%, the 30-year breached 5.7%, and the Fed raised rates at the September 15-16 meeting for the first time in three years on a unanimous vote, with roughly 70% implied odds of a further 25bp increase by year-end against about a 19% chance for October. WTI near $90 and Brent above $101 reflect a continuing Strait of Hormuz tanker campaign, with at least seven reported attacks in the past week, even as Gulf exports have recovered to roughly 18.3 million barrels per day. Index concentration is extreme, with Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft above 21% of the S&P 500 and Nvidia near a $6 trillion market value. The identifiable risk window is the September FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC, preceded by a 10-year auction at 17:00 UTC. A hawkish read into an already stretched long end is the credible delayed-second-leg mechanism, so Tail is lifted into the watch band for 18:00-21:00 UTC and then eased as price discovery completes. Shared Finviz context was read and found stale, dated 2026-09-29 with partial collection status, so it was excluded and the assessment rests on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 published hours to 04:00 UTC, Claude Tail ranged from 8 to 22 and the mapped state was EA_ON in 22 of 24 hours. Tail built from 8 through the European morning of Oct 6 into a 19-22 peak across the 14:00-16:00 UTC U.S. session window, the only stretch mapped to WATCH, with dominant mode recorded as trend-up from 10:00 to 19:00 UTC. From the 20:00 UTC cash close onward Tail eased back to a 10-14 range and mode reverted to mixed, where it has stayed through the Asian session. Stress held in a narrow 45-48 elevated band throughout and Confidence stayed high at 86-88.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail in the low band through the European session and the U.S. cash open, rising gradually from 10 to 19 as liquidity and event proximity build. It enters the watch band only for 18:00-21:00 UTC, peaking at 24 in the hour after the September FOMC minutes, which is where a yield-led delayed second leg would appear if the minutes read hawkish into a 24-year-high long end. Tail never reaches the block threshold, consistent with scoring observed structure rather than hypothetical post-event alignment. From 21:00 UTC the path decays back toward the overnight baseline, reaching 11 by the final slot, and Confidence steps down from 88 to 77 as the assessment ages.
